title: We’re Late, Sam
山姆，我們晚了
paras: Sam Okafor, her busiest {{client|client}}, walked into Rachel Gomez’s office without an appointment, holding a plastic tea infuser. “Someone is selling copies of my product,” he said, “under almost the same name.” Rachel had been the lawyer for his startup, Kettlebloom, since its first month, and she knew he had never registered anything. “I’ll be honest,” she said. “We’re late.”
山姆・奧卡佛是她最忙的客戶，沒有預約就走進蕾秋・戈麥斯的辦公室，手裡拿著一個塑膠泡茶器。「有人在賣我產品的仿冒品，」他說，「名稱還幾乎一模一樣。」蕾秋從他的新創公司「茶花盛開」成立的第一個月起就擔任他們的律師，她知道他什麼都沒登記過。「我跟你說實話，」她說。「我們晚了。」

First she checked the name. Kettlebloom had never been registered as a {{trademark|trademark}}, so the copycat could claim a right to something similar. “Now the design,” she said. “Did you apply for a {{patent|patent}} on the infuser?” Sam looked at the floor. “I was going to.” Then Rachel pulled out his agreement with the freelancer who had drawn the logo. The {{copyright|copyright}} still belonged to the designer, because nobody had put a transfer in writing. “I’ll {{obtain|obtain}} a signed transfer from her tomorrow,” Rachel said. “She likes you. She’ll agree.”
她先查了名稱。「茶花盛開」從來沒有註冊成商標，所以仿冒者可以主張自己對類似的名稱也有權利。「接著是設計，」她說。「你有為這個泡茶器申請專利嗎？」山姆低頭看著地板。「我本來打算要申請的。」接著蕾秋抽出他和繪製標誌的自由接案設計師簽的合約。版權仍然屬於設計師，因為沒有人把轉讓的事寫成書面。「明天我會向她取得一份簽署好的轉讓書，」蕾秋說。「她喜歡你，會同意的。」

That afternoon Rachel wrote to the online marketplace to {{inquire|inquire}} who was behind the shop. Her letter was polite and firm. She {{enclose|enclosed}} the filing receipts for both applications and asked the marketplace to {{terminate|terminate}} the seller’s account if the listings stayed up. Two weeks later they were gone. Sam sent her flowers, and she sent him her bill.
那天下午，蕾秋寫信給網路商城，詢問那家店背後是誰。她的信措辭客氣但態度堅定。她隨信附上兩項申請的送件收據，並要求商城如果那些商品頁面還掛著，就終止該賣家的帳號。兩週後，那些頁面全都不見了。山姆送了她一束花，她則寄給他帳單。
